params.name: scope
params.description: Slice granularity the signal was detected on: `account` (whole brand), `account_platform` (brand on one AI platform), `topic`, or `topic_platform`.

params.name: platform
params.description: AI platform the signal was detected on (e.g. `OpenAI`). Multi-platform signals carry the `(multi)` sentinel; the response `slice.platforms` lists the real platforms.

params.name: metric
params.description: Metric the signal fired on. Known values: `presence_rate`, `position_top_rate`, `cited_domain_rate` (new metrics may be added).

params.name: tier
params.description: Confidence tier. When omitted, only the default user-facing tiers are returned (`high`, `confident`, `worth_a_look`, `provisional`); pass an explicit tier to see a single tier, including the noise-floor tiers (`low_confidence`, `underpowered`, `untested`).

params.name: subject_kind
params.description: Whose movement the signal describes: your `brand` or a `competitor`.

params.name: mover_url
params.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against the URLs in the signal's `url_movers` evidence (per-URL citation movers, emitted for `cited_domain_rate` signals). Only signals with at least one matching mover URL are returned; signals without URL movers never match.

params.name: sort
params.description: Sort order: `score_desc` (engine priority, default), `delta_desc` (largest absolute change first), or `detected_desc` (newest first).

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of signals to return.

items.docs:
List detected signals for a brand — statistically-tested movements (level changes and trends) in AI-visibility metrics, produced by the nightly detection sweep.

## Population

By default only user-facing signals are returned: the confidence tiers `high`, `confident`, `worth_a_look`, and `provisional`. Pass an explicit `tier` to select a single tier, including the noise-floor tiers. An ongoing signal is re-detected daily under the same `fingerprint`; a multi-day date range returns only the lates

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of dates to return.

items.docs: List recent distinct detection dates (`detected_for_date`) that produced user-facing signals, newest first. Useful for building date pickers or polling for new detection runs — the population matches `listSignals` with default filters, so every returned day has at least one signal.

params.name: fingerprint
params.description: Only reactions on this signal fingerprint.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of reactions to return.

items.docs: List reactions users have set on this brand's signals, newest first. This is **brand-wide** — it returns every user's reactions, not just the caller's — so an integration can export the team's aggregate feedback. Filter by `fingerprint` to get reactions for one signal identity, or by `reaction` to get e.g. everything marked `useful`.

Fetch one signal by ID, including its full narrative (what happened, why it matters, what to do) when available. Returns 404 for IDs that exist but are not user-facing (non-fired or cluster-child rows) — the same population rule as `listSignals`.

Set (or replace) the calling user's reaction on a signal. Reactions are keyed on the signal's stable `fingerprint`, so a reaction survives the nightly re-detection of the same underlying issue.

Requires a **user token** (JWT) — API keys have no user identity to attribute the reaction to and receive 403.
Remove the calling user's reaction on a signal's stable identity. Requires a **user token** (JWT); API keys receive 403.
